item: Max-norm semigroup via star averaging (random triangle removal): A/D = P + R with P = sum of star averages = UV, VU = I + W, ||exp(-sP)||_inf <= 1+2s, plus a mixed-norm (l_inf head / l2 remainder) Dyson expansion giving sup_{s<=log n} ||exp(-sA/D)||_inf <= C1 (1+log n)^J
item_type: lemma (F5 change of representation edge space -> vertex space, F2 flavour)
lean_status_why: The paper's P = UV factorization, the bound ||exp(-sP)||_inf <= 1+2s, the mixed-norm perturbation expansion and the uniform semigroup bound are all formalized (graph_star_semigroup_bound, goodPrefix_semigroup_quantitative, goodPrefix_uniform_semigroup) and lie on the comparator's proof path; in addition the Lean re-derives the device a second time, in discrete time on a shrinking edge set, for its self-contained prefix.
lean_gaps: Text-level only: the Lean was NOT compiled (no local toolchain); dependency chains come from scripts/extract_lean.py name resolution (data/items/188_lean.json) plus hand reading.

Route for ||exp(-sP)||_inf <= 1+2s: the paper uses the push-through identity (UV)^j = U(VU)^{j-1}V and E0(s) = Id - U int_0^s e^{-v(Id+W)} dv V; the Lean (star_semigroup_bound) applies an abstract rectangular_semigroup_bound to U, V = starAverage U and W = V*U - 1 with ||W|| <= 1 (starAverage_neighbor_norm). Same content, slightly different packaging.

The abstract Lean lemma star_semigroup_bound hard-codes row sum 2 (each edge has exactly two endpoints) and 0/1 entries. It does not cover hypergraph incidence (row sum r >= 3), where ||W||_inf = r-1 > 1 and the one-line bound fails (see negative controls).

Mixed-norm Dyson expansion: Lean states it abstractly over an algebra hom into continuous linear maps (Stability/Volterra.lean:190 perturbation_mixed_norm_bound) with explicit constants; the final bound is C1(1+log n)^{2K+1} with K > 4/gamma, versus the paper's unspecified J.

Quasirandomness input differs in constants: Lean's GoodPrefixGraph uses c = 1/80000-type exponents and cycle length 8000 (prefixSpectralError), with the prefix proved in Lean rather than cited from Joos-Kuhn.

Reuse signal, precisely: the Lean prefix (uniform_prefix_obligation) does NOT call graph_star_semigroup_bound, star_semigroup_bound or perturbation_mixed_norm_bound. It re-implements the device as movingStarMean/movingStarLift (P_k = U V_k on a nested active set), movingStar_trajectory_representation (x = M - U b with a vertex trajectory b), movingStarResponse_linf (bound 1 + 2 sum a_k) and movingStar_mixed_stability (discrete mixed-norm absorption via moving_perturbation_mixed_norm_absorb). Declarations shared by the two uses are only globalStarAverage, globalLinkAdjacency and graph_star_approximation. So the second use re-derives the same device in a new setting (moving support, discrete time); it is not a library call.

graph_star_approximation (Spectral/GraphStarApproximation.lean:26), listed in the shortlist hint, is the trace-method step (cycle counts give ||A/D - J/N||_2 small, Chung-Graham style). It is an ingredient for R's l2 bound, classical in substance, not the device itself. Both the continuation (via goodPrefix_star_approximation) and the prefix (via density_global_spectral) use it.

Comparator is exact (sharp_terminal_leave = paper Thm main, all three parts). No statement mentions the semigroup, so the device is visible only as an internal lemma (dominated share 0.035 for goodPrefix_uniform_semigroup; 0.032 for movingStar_mixed_stability; the whole prefix cone uniform_prefix_obligation 0.269).
Family 188 is absent from lean/formalization.yaml (comparator present in ComparatorChallenges and docs/188.md).

lean_source.name: incidenceDegree
lean_source.text:
def incidenceDegree {ι κ : Type*} [Fintype ι] (U : Matrix ι κ ℝ) (v : κ) : ℝ :=
  ∑ e, U e v

lean_source.name: starAverage
lean_source.text:
noncomputable def starAverage {ι κ : Type*} [Fintype ι] (U : Matrix ι κ ℝ) :
    Matrix κ ι ℝ := fun v e => U e v / incidenceDegree U v

lean_source.name: star_semigroup_bound
lean_source.text:
theorem star_semigroup_bound {ι κ : Type*} [Fintype ι] [Fintype κ]
    [DecidableEq ι] [DecidableEq κ] [Nonempty ι] [Nonempty κ]
    (U : Matrix ι κ ℝ) (hU : ∀ e v, 0 ≤ U e v)
    (hidem : ∀ e v, U e v * U e v = U e v)
    (hrow : ∀ e, ∑ v, U e v = 2)
    (hdeg : ∀ v, 0 < incidenceDegree U v) (s : ℝ) (hs : 0 ≤ s) :
    ‖NormedSpace.exp ((-s) • (U * starAverage U))‖ ≤ 1 + 2 * s

lean_source.name: edgeIncidence
lean_source.text:
noncomputable def edgeIncidence {n : ℕ} (G : Graph n) : Matrix G (Fin n) ℝ :=
  fun e u => if u ∈ e.val then 1 else 0

lean_source.name: globalLinkAdjacency
lean_source.text:
noncomputable def globalLinkAdjacency {n : ℕ} (G : Graph n) (hG : G ⊆ completeGraph n) :
    Matrix G G ℝ := ∑ u, extendStar (edgeStar G u) (linkStarMatrix G hG u)

lean_source.name: globalStarAverage
lean_source.text:
noncomputable def globalStarAverage {n : ℕ} (G : Graph n) : Matrix G G ℝ :=
  ∑ u, extendStar (edgeStar G u) averagingProjector

lean_source.name: globalStarAverage_factorization
lean_source.text:
theorem globalStarAverage_factorization {n : ℕ} (G : Graph n)
    (hG : G ⊆ completeGraph n) :
    globalStarAverage G = edgeIncidence G * starAverage (edgeIncidence G)

lean_source.name: graph_star_semigroup_bound
lean_source.text:
theorem graph_star_semigroup_bound {n : ℕ} [NeZero n] (G : Graph n)
    [Nonempty G] (hG : G ⊆ completeGraph n) (hdeg : ∀ u, 0 < currentDegree G u)
    (s : ℝ) (hs : 0 ≤ s) :
    ‖NormedSpace.exp ((-s) • globalStarAverage G)‖ ≤ 1 + 2*s

lean_source.name: goodPrefix_semigroup_quantitative
lean_source.text:
theorem goodPrefix_semigroup_quantitative {n : ℕ} [NeZero n] {G : Graph n} [Nonempty G]
    {c C : ℝ} (h : GoodPrefixGraph n c C G) (hne : ∀ u, (neighbors G u).Nonempty)
    (hD : 1 ≤ prefixD n) (hδ : (n : ℝ)^(-c) ≤ 1)
    (T : ℝ) (hT : 0 ≤ T) (K : ℕ) (s : ℝ) (hs : s ∈ Set.Icc (0 : ℝ) T) :
    ‖NormedSpace.exp ((-s) • ((prefixD n)⁻¹ • globalLinkAdjacency G h.1))‖ ≤
      (∑ j ∈ Finset.range K, ((1+2*T)*6*T)^j*(1+2*T)) +
      Real.sqrt G.card * ((2*prefixSpectralError n c*T)^K *
        Real.exp (T*(2*prefixSpectralError n c)))

lean_source.name: goodPrefix_uniform_semigroup
lean_source.text:
theorem goodPrefix_uniform_semigroup {c : ℝ} (hc : 0 < c) :
    ∃ C₁ : ℝ, 0 < C₁ ∧ ∃ J : ℕ, ∀ᶠ n : ℕ in atTop,
      ∀ (C : ℝ) (G : Graph n) (h : GoodPrefixGraph n c C G),
      ∀ s ∈ Set.Icc (0 : ℝ) (Real.log n),
        ‖NormedSpace.exp ((-s) • ((prefixD n)⁻¹ • globalLinkAdjacency G h.1))‖ ≤
          C₁*(1+Real.log n)^J

lean_source.name: graph_star_approximation
lean_source.text:
theorem graph_star_approximation (n : ℕ) (hr : Even (n+3)) (D δ : ℝ)
    (hD : 1 ≤ D) (hδ0 : 0 ≤ δ) (hδ1 : δ ≤ 1)
    (hrow : ∀ x : V, |((Finset.univ.filter (G.Adj x)).card : ℝ) - D| ≤ δ*D)
    (hmain : |((graphEmbeddings (SimpleGraph.cycleGraph (n+3)) G).card : ℝ) - D^(n+3)| ≤
      δ * D^(n+3))
    (hcyc : ∀ b, 3 ≤ b → b < n+3 →
      ((graphEmbeddings (SimpleGraph.cycleGraph b) G).card : ℝ) ≤ 2 * D^b) :
    ‖D⁻¹ • G.adjMatrix ℝ - averagingProjector‖ ≤
      4 * (((n+4 : ℕ) : ℝ) * δ + ((n+3 : ℕ) : ℝ)^(n+4) * 2^(n+3) *
        ((Fintype.card V : ℝ) / D^((n+3)/2) + 1/D)) ^ (1 / ((n+3 : ℕ) : ℝ)) + 7*δ

lean_source.name: movingStarMean
lean_source.text:
noncomputable def movingStarMean {E V : Type*} [Fintype E] [Fintype V]
    (ends : E → Finset V) (active : Finset E) (x : E → ℝ) (u : V) : ℝ := by
  classical
  exact (∑ e ∈ active.filter (fun e => u ∈ ends e), x e) / movingStarDegree ends active u

lean_source.name: movingStarLift
lean_source.text:
noncomputable def movingStarLift {E V : Type*} [Fintype E] [Fintype V]
    (ends : E → Finset V) (b : V → ℝ) (e : E) : ℝ := ∑ u ∈ ends e, b u

lean_source.name: movingStar_trajectory_representation
lean_source.text:
theorem movingStar_trajectory_representation {E V : Type*} [Fintype E] [Fintype V]
    (ends : E → Finset V) (active : ℕ → Finset E) (a : ℕ → ℝ)
    (M x : ℕ → E → ℝ) (T : ℕ)
    (hnest : ∀ k < T, active (k+1) ⊆ active k)
    (hinit : ∀ e ∈ active 0, x 0 e = M 0 e)
    (hstep : ∀ k < T, ∀ e ∈ active (k+1), x (k+1) e = x k e -
      a k*movingStarLift ends (movingStarMean ends (active k) (x k)) e + (M (k+1) e-M k e)) :
    ∀ e ∈ active T, x T e = M T e-movingStarLift ends (movingStarVertices ends active a M T) e

lean_source.name: movingStarResponse_linf
lean_source.text:
lemma movingStarResponse_linf {E V : Type*} [Fintype E] [Fintype V]
    (ends : E → Finset V) (hends : ∀ e, (ends e).card = 2)
    (active : ℕ → Finset E) (a : ℕ → ℝ) (T : ℕ)
    (hnest : ∀ k < T, active (k+1) ⊆ active k)
    (ha : ∀ k < T, 0 ≤ a k ∧ a k ≤ 1) (M : ℕ → E → ℝ) :
    trajectorySeminorm (fun t => activeLinf (active t)) T (movingStarResponse ends active a M) ≤
      (1+2*∑ k ∈ Finset.range T, a k)*trajectorySeminorm (fun t => activeLinf (active t)) T M

lean_source.name: movingStar_mixed_stability
lean_source.text:
theorem movingStar_mixed_stability {E V : Type*} [Fintype E] [Fintype V]
    (ends : E → Finset V) (hends : ∀ e, (ends e).card = 2)
    (active : ℕ → Finset E) (a : ℕ → ℝ) (R : ℕ → Module.End ℝ (E → ℝ))
    (M x : ℕ → E → ℝ) (T K : ℕ)
    (hnest : ∀ k < T, active (k+1) ⊆ active k)
    (ha : ∀ k < T, 0 ≤ a k ∧ a k ≤ 1)
    (hinit : ∀ e ∈ active 0, x 0 e = M 0 e)
    (hstep : ∀ k < T, ∀ e ∈ active (k+1), x (k+1) e = x k e -
      a k*(movingStarLift ends (movingStarMean ends (active k) (x k)) e+R k (x k) e) +
        (M (k+1) e-M k e))
    {B δ : ℝ} (hB : 0 ≤ B) (hδ : 0 ≤ δ)
    (hRinf : ∀ k < T, ∀ z, activeLinf (active k) (R k z) ≤ B*activeLinf (active k) z)
    (hR₂ : ∀ k < T, ∀ z, activeL2 (active k) (R k z) ≤ δ*activeL2 (active k) z)
    (hK : ((1+2*∑ k ∈ Finset.range T, a k)*(∑ k ∈ Finset.range T, a k)*δ)^K*
      (Fintype.card E : ℝ) ≤ 1/2) :
    trajectorySeminorm (fun t => activeLinf (active t)) T x ≤
      2*(∑ j ∈ Finset.range K,
        ((1+2*∑ k ∈ Finset.range T, a k)*(∑ k ∈ Finset.range T, a k)*B)^j)*
        (1+2*∑ k ∈ Finset.range T, a k)*trajectorySeminorm (fun t => activeLinf (active t)) T M

lean_source.name: prefix_centered_edge_recurrence
lean_source.text:
lemma prefix_centered_edge_recurrence {n i : ℕ} (ω : History (Graph n) (prefixTime n))
    (hω : ω ∈ (historyLaw (PMF.pure (completeGraph n)) (fun _ => step) (prefixTime n) (prefixTime n)).support)
    (hi : i < prefixTime n) (hs : earlyTemplateScale 1 2 n i ≠ 0)
    (e : CompleteEdge n) (he : e ∈ graphActive (ω (historyIndex (prefixTime n) (i+1)))) :
    prefixCenteredEdge ω (i+1) e = prefixCenteredEdge ω i e-
      prefixEdgeRate ω i*(movingStarLift (fun e : CompleteEdge n => e.val)
        (movingStarMean (fun e : CompleteEdge n => e.val)
          (graphActive (ω (historyIndex (prefixTime n) i))) (prefixCenteredEdge ω i)) e+
        prefixEdgeResidual ω hω i (prefixCenteredEdge ω i) e)+
      (prefixEdgeForcing ω (i+1) e-prefixEdgeForcing ω i e)

speedup_targets.title: Triangle-removal prefix: codegree tracking to density n^{-1/2+eps} (BFL 2015 tracking / Joos-Kuhn specialised to triangles)
speedup_targets.statement: Run random triangle removal from K_n to density p = n^{-1/2+eps}. With failure probability <= exp(-(log n)^{4/3}), every codegree is (1 +- n^{-c}) times its prediction, every degree likewise, and link-cycle and rooted-extension counts are as predicted. Lean form: OAI.SharpTerminalLeave.uniform_prefix_obligation (Tracking/NormalizedTrackingAbsolute.lean:84); key internal step prefix_edge_barrier_improvement (Process/CenteredEdgeVectorTriangle.lean:19).
speedup_targets.reference: Bohman-Frieze-Lubetzky, Random triangle removal, Adv. Math. 280 (2015), arXiv:1203.4223 (tracking part); Joos-Kuhn, The hypergraph removal process, arXiv:2412.15039 (the paper's black box); Lean: OAI TriangleRemoval prefix cone.
speedup_targets.status: known (BFL for triangles; JK in general); proved in the OAI Lean by the moving-star device
speedup_targets.current_size: BFL ~45 pp. total, most of it tracking; JK ~87 pp. (general F). Lean: prefix cone 623 decls / 8,837 lines (452 decls / 6,991 lines exclusive); the moving-star device files are ~940 lines (MovingStarDegree 327, ActiveL2Map 342, MovingResidualForcing 171, MovingPerturbationFiniteExpansion 96).
speedup_targets.how_item_helps: BFL needed scalar self-correcting martingales for every codegree, plus carefully designed triangular extensions to pass the n^{7/4} barrier. With the device, the whole centred codegree vector x_k obeys x_{k+1} = x_k - a_k(P_k + R_k)x_k + noise, where P_k is a moving star average, ||R_k||_2 is small from link spectra and ||R_k||_inf <= 6. movingStar_mixed_stability turns this into an l_inf barrier improvement in one step, so self-correction becomes a single linear stability statement instead of a per-variable drift analysis.
speedup_targets.expected_speedup: high (within Lean: give vs withhold the movingStar_* lemmas and graph_star_approximation; otherwise the prover must build per-codegree self-correcting martingales)
speedup_targets.caveat: Same family, same model, same process: this is the in-family reuse the shortlist cites, NOT a held-out test. It shows the device adapts to moving supports and discrete time.

open_problems.title: Final size of the H-free process for strictly 2-balanced H (C_4-free, K_4-free)
open_problems.statement: Bohman-Keevash conjecture: the H-free process ends with Theta(n^{2-(v_H-2)/(e_H-1)} (log n)^{1/(e_H-1)}) edges whp.
open_problems.reference: Bohman-Keevash, The early evolution of the H-free process, Invent. Math. 181 (2010), arXiv:0908.0429; Warnke, When does the K_4-free process stop?, RSA 44 (2014), arXiv:1007.3037; Picollelli, The final size of the C_4-free process, CPC 20 (2011).
open_problems.status: open in general (known for some H, partly up to constants; not re-verified this session)
open_problems.obstruction_match: Matching lower bounds need tracking of open-pair statistics to the end, a self-correction problem of the same linear-stability type. However the H-free process adds edges instead of removing them, so its drift operator differs.
open_problems.adaptation_sketch: Write the drift of the open-pair vector and check whether its leading part factors through vertex space. For H = C_4, pairs in a potential C_4 can be disjoint, so it probably does not.

lean_feasibility.score: statable with < 300 lines of new definitions

open_problems.title: R(3,k) lower-bound constant via steered triangle-free processes
open_problems.statement: Improve R(3,k) >= c k^2/log k beyond the 2025 constants (1/3 by Campos-Jenssen-Michelen-Sahasrabudhe; 1/2 claimed in 'Improving R(3,k) in just two bites').
open_problems.reference: arXiv:2505.13371 https://arxiv.org/abs/2505.13371 ; arXiv:2510.19718 https://arxiv.org/abs/2510.19718 (seen only via search snippets this session)
open_problems.obstruction_match: Weak. CJMS explicitly avoid martingale self-correction by steering the process. A linear l_inf stability tool would be an alternative way to analyse denser steered processes. The analogy is superficial unless the steered process's tracked vector has star structure.
open_problems.adaptation_sketch: Identify the codegree-type vector in the steered process and test whether its linearization is star-averaged.

lean_feasibility.statable_with: Ramsey numbers and the steered process construction

theorem_corollaries: Bohman-Frieze-Lubetzky 2015 Theorem 1 (F_n = n^{3/2+o(1)} whp) and the Bollobas-Erdős Theta(n^{3/2}) conjecture follow from the sharp theorem. These are corollaries, not device reuse.
Erdős problem #1155 (erdosproblems.com/1155) asks whether E F_n is of order n^{3/2}, among finer questions. The sharp L^2 statement answers the question about the mean (corollary).
Joos-Kuhn Conjecture 16.2 for F = K_3 (convergence in probability) is the theorem itself.
release_reuse: Inside 188 only. The device is re-derived for the Lean-only prefix (a moving star average on a nested active edge set, in discrete time): movingStar_mixed_stability, movingStarResponse_linf, movingStar_trajectory_representation. This is a genuine second application to a different statement (codegree tracking, i.e. the JK black box). But it was made by the same model on the same problem, and implemented as fresh code rather than as a call to graph_star_semigroup_bound.

Grep over lean/OAI for starAverage|movingStar|globalStarAverage|edgeIncidence outside TriangleRemoval: no hits. No other family in the release uses the device, and CONTENTS.md lists no other random-greedy or removal-process family.

negative_controls.setting: Random greedy processes with bounded degree (D = O(1)), e.g. greedy matching/independent set on random d-regular graphs with fixed d
negative_controls.reason: The naive bound ||exp(-sA/D)||_inf <= e^{s||A/D||_inf} already costs only O(1) over the relevant time, so the device gives no gain.

negative_controls.setting: Hypergraph incidence with r >= 3 ends per edge (abstract star_semigroup_bound with row sum r)
negative_controls.reason: VU = I + W with ||W||_inf = r-1 > 1, so exp(-v(I+W)) is not l_inf-contractive and the one-line bound fails. The Lean lemma hard-codes row sum 2.
negative_controls.expected: device fails as stated (a proved-false analogue of the one-line bound)

negative_controls.reason: Edges of a common K_4 can be disjoint, so A is not a sum of star (link) matrices and P no longer approximates A/D in l2.
negative_controls.expected: device does not apply without new ideas

negative_controls.setting: Any argument that needs only l2 control (spectral-gap mixing, l2 stability)
negative_controls.reason: P is PSD, so ||exp(-sP)||_2 <= 1 is trivial; the device's content is the l_inf bound.

top5.title: Triangle-removal prefix (uniform_prefix_obligation / prefix_edge_barrier_improvement)
top5.argument: This is the only place where the device demonstrably did work on a statement other than its own proposition: the Lean replaces the paper's JK black box (87 pp.) with codegree-vector stability driven by a moving star average. Everything needed is already defined in OAI, and the OAI proof gives a size baseline. Run the speedup test by giving vs withholding the movingStar_* lemmas (and graph_star_approximation). Caveat: same model and same process, so this is reuse evidence, not a held-out discoverability test.

top5.title: Uniform semigroup proposition without the star factorization (ablation)
top5.argument: Calibration arm. Withholding graph_star_semigroup_bound should force e^{O(D)} losses or a long detour, which measures how much of the proposition the factorization carries. It is the item's own result, so it cannot confirm a jump.

top5.title: Random triangle removal from quasirandom starting graphs
top5.argument: The closest genuinely new statement. The continuation needs only quasirandom link data, and so does the moving-star prefix. It is statable in OAI with a ~40-line hypothesis, and the device should transfer almost verbatim. A short proof would be a clean downstream demonstration, but it is close to a corollary of the method, so treat it as low-novelty transfer.

top5.title: Triangle-free process tracking (Bohman 2009 / Bohman-Keevash / FGM)
top5.lean: statable with < 300 lines of new definitions
top5.argument: The best external speedup candidate: a long, famous self-correction analysis of edge-indexed statistics with triangle-induced interactions. Whether its drift operator is star-averaged has not been checked. If it is, the device could shorten the tracking substantially.

top5.title: Fluctuations of F_n
top5.argument: Open, and statable now with OAI definitions. The obstruction (uniform l_inf linear response) is exactly what the device controls. The payoff would be a new theorem rather than a shorter proof.
